title: Wander: The Cult of Barnacle Bay - Take a Look
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xvdkNKQAbJ8

Daniel (@dungeondive) unboxes **Wander: The Cult of Barnacle Bay** (Panda Cult Games) the day it arrives — the second game off his most-anticipated list of 2019 to land. The box promises Elder Bane and his converts: crab-crazed otter fishermen, tentacle-armed rabbit zealots, fish-bat casters and bear-shark brutes, loose in a fishing village that one to five heroes must take back.

He spends the opening minutes being unusually honest about the theme. Anthropomorphic animals were his entire childhood — he can date it to finding a Ninja Turtles comic on a food-court magazine stand around 1985, and the RPG a year later — but he drifted away, and he's candid that some of the drift is stigma he isn't sure he should have absorbed. He also flatly rejects the "kids' game" dismissal: nearly everything he owns is a kids' game, and he's fine with that.

What excites him is structural. The campaign book branches — the intro scenario opens onto three different follow-ups — which he notes most games of this type simply don't do. Tarot-sized event cards carry non-combat skill checks, the bosses have AI decks, and the rulebook is a manageable 40 pages in rectangle format, a detail he admits he raises more than any other reviewer alive. His one worry: only four or five grunt types in the base game.

----

Daniel talks himself out of a genre bias on camera here. Has a theme ever kept you off a game you later loved?
